design.text: Randomized, placebo-controlled trial with an open-label induction phase (three sequential doses of fluconazole 150 mg every 72 hours on Days 1, 4 and 7) and an 11-week maintenance phase; patients randomized 2:1 to VIVJOA 150 mg or placebo.

citations.quote: Trial 1 and Trial 2 were both randomized, placebo-controlled trials evaluating the efficacy and safety of VIVJOA in the reduction of RVVC. Both trials consisted of two phases: an open-label induction phase and an 11-week maintenance phase. Patients received three sequential doses of 150 mg of fluconazole (every 72 hours) on Days, 1, 4 and 7 during the induction phase. Patients returned 14 days after the first dose of fluconazole and if the acute VVC episode was resolved (vulvovaginal
signs and symptoms score < 3) they were randomized (2:1) to receive either 150 mg of VIVJOA or placebo for 7 days followed by 11 weekly doses in the maintenance phase.

indication.text: VIVJOA is an azole antifungal indicated to reduce the incidence of recurrent vulvovaginal candidiasis (RVVC) in females with a history of RVVC who are NOT of reproductive potential.

citations.quote: VIVJOA is indicated to reduce the incidence of recurrent vulvovaginal candidiasis (RVVC) in females with a history of RVVC who are NOT of reproductive potential [see *Warnings and Precautions* (5.1), *Use in Specific Populations* (8.3), and *Clinical Studies* (14)].

target_moa.text: Oteseconazole is an azole antifungal that inhibits fungal lanosterol demethylase (CYP51 / sterol 14-alpha demethylase), blocking conversion of lanosterol to ergosterol required for fungal cell membrane formation.

citations.quote: Oteseconazole (VT-1161, OTE) is an azole antifungal metalloenzyme inhibitor targeting the fungal sterol, 14\alpha demethylase (CYP51), which mediates fungal membrane permeability.

Mechanism of action	Oteseconazole inhibits fungal lanosterol demethylase (CYP51) which catalyzes an early step in the conversion of lanosterol to ergosterol, which is required for fungal cell wall formation.
Oteseconazole (VT-1161, OTE) is an azole antifungal metalloenzyme inhibitor targeting the fungal sterol, 14\alpha demethylase (CYP51), which mediates fungal membrane permeability.

key_safety.text: Most frequently reported adverse reactions (incidence >2%) were headache (7.4%) and nausea (3.6%). One of 580 (0.2%) VIVJOA-treated patients discontinued due to an adverse reaction (allergic dermatitis).

citations.quote: The most frequently reported adverse reactions (incidence >2%) among VIVJOA-treated patients in Trial 1, Trial 2 and Trial 3 were headache (includes headache, migraines, sinus headaches) (7.4%) and nausea (3.6%).
The adverse reaction that led to discontinuation in 1 of 580 (0.2%) VIVJOA-treated patients was allergic dermatitis.
